saints.name: St. Chad
saints.title: Bishop of Lichfield
saints.shortBlurb: A disciple of St. Aidan who yielded his see in humility, then evangelized the Mercians on foot from his new seat at Lichfield…
biography: Chad, or Ceadda, a Northumbrian, was trained at Lindisfarne under St. Aidan and completed his formation among the monasteries of Ireland. When his brother Cedd died of the plague in 664, Chad succeeded him as abbot of Lastingham in Yorkshire.

That same year King Oswiu named him bishop of the Northumbrians, and he was consecrated by Wini of the West Saxons with two British bishops. When Wilfrid, the see's chosen bishop, returned from Gaul, Archbishop Theodore of Canterbury judged Chad's position irregular. Chad yielded it without protest and went back to Lastingham, and Theodore, struck by such humility, confirmed his ordination.

Later in 669 King Wulfhere of Mercia asked for a bishop, and Theodore sent Chad to the Mercians and the people of Lindsey; he fixed his see at Lichfield. He travelled his vast diocese on foot until Theodore ordered him to ride, once lifting him into the saddle with his own hands.

He had labored among the Mercians only two and a half years when he died in the plague on 2 March 672. Bede, who tells his story in the Ecclesiastical History, judged that Chad and his brother Cedd together had won Mercia to the faith.
saints.knownFor: Evangelizing Mercia from his see at Lichfield.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 2 March
